Icon

Line-icon primitive — the single source of truth for iconography. 24×24 grid, 2px stroke, inherits currentColor. Pass to Button/IconButton via icon. Returns null for an unknown name, so a typo fails visibly in review rather than rendering a broken glyph.

Live example

The example needs JavaScript; the usage below shows the markup.

Usage

The single source of truth for iconography — 97 line glyphs from Lucide (ISC), drawn on a 24×24 grid with a 2px stroke, inheriting currentColor so icons take the colour of surrounding text.

<Icon name="graduation-cap" size={24} />
<Icon name="map-pin" title="Unidade mais próxima" />

// Inside action components:
<Button variant="primary" icon={<Icon name="arrow-right" />}>Quero me inscrever</Button>
<IconButton ariaLabel="Buscar unidades" icon={<Icon name="search" />} />

Size with size (default 20; 24 in buttons and navigation, 16 inside dense tables).

Reach for these first on this brand's surfaces: graduation-cap, school, book-open (programmes and levels), map-pin, building-2, navigation (units), file-text, clipboard-check, upload, id-card, calendar-check (enrollment), chart-column, trending-up, target (results and the IDE-Sesc), sparkles, brain, bot (the Sab.IA platform). The full list is the IconName union in Icon.d.ts.

Accessibility: an icon with no title renders aria-hidden — correct for decoration beside a text label. Pass title (in pt-BR) only when the icon carries meaning on its own; if it sits inside an IconButton, label the button instead. An unknown name renders nothing, so a typo shows up as a missing icon in review rather than a broken glyph.

Never hand-draw an icon or paste a one-off SVG into a page. Icon.js is generated from the vendored SVGs — vendor the glyph you need and re-run the generator (assets/icons/README.md). Edits made directly to Icon.js are overwritten.

CSS classes

Renders no class contract of its own (generated artwork or a function library).
